citation: Troitzsch and Hamacher (2020). Control-oriented Thermal Building Modelling. https://doi.org/10.36227/techrxiv.11923587
description: CoBMo is a Python building model maintained in the mesmo-dev repository for formulating model predictive control problems with linear, convex equations. It relates electricity use by thermal building systems to indoor climate, accounting for interactions with occupants, appliances and the environment. Implemented components cover thermal comfort and indoor air quality, with documented contributions for storage, ventilation and hydronic radiators. The repository provides simulation and optimisation examples and YAML configuration. Coverage is the user's building and control horizon, without a fixed national stock or measurement period. Source is public and free under MIT. Execution needs Python 3.9 and an optimisation solver such as Gurobi or CPLEX under separate terms. The README warns that interfaces may change, and the setup guide provides a tested environment as a fallback for dependency incompatibilities. A further limitation is that the linear formulation limits the physical behaviour represented. CoBMo supports building-load flexibility and control studies and complements detailed EnergyPlus simulation (model-energyplus) with a control-oriented representation. No solver or building case was run here.
